<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

A pod template is a folder at any path a command names (the main repo or governance); a pod is the running group made from it, with its own folder under `community/pods/<pod>/` on the governance branch. Memory is filed per role and subject, and a new pod can start without earlier pods' memory.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Define a recurring group of seats once, as files, and keep each running pod's record in governance.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Starting and stopping pods (plans 248, 249); shipped templates and adopt (PRD 010).

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Cost: on demand only: reading a template is in-process; writing a pod folder is the writer's usual commit. No loop, poll or timer.
- No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
- Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
